projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

This benign anomaly suggests a quick router reboot or network scan to clear phantom connections and prevent alert fatigue.

The persistently high device count (22–26) paired with zero camera motion throughout the evening strongly indicates a false positive in the presence detection system, likely caused by neighbor devices, IoT network noise, or a scanning glitch rather than actual occupancy. This matters because it may be triggering unnecessary automations or masking real security events, so a network diagnostic or presence threshold adjustment is recommended.

The sustained 22–26 'mobile device' count alongside zero camera motion strongly suggests a network reporting anomaly (likely IoT devices being misclassified as mobile) rather than actual occupancy, given the household size. Steve should verify the UniFi dashboard to rule out phantom connections or confirm if guests are gathered in a camera-blind zone.

The combination of a sustained 22–26 device count with zero camera motion on a Friday evening indicates a likely network probing anomaly or unregistered guests, since the household of six wouldn't naturally generate this many connections. This cross-signal gap warrants verifying camera functionality and checking for unexpected visitors.

The sustained count of 22–27 connected devices alongside zero camera motion during a typical Friday evening strongly indicates Wi-Fi multipath interference or 'ghost' connections rather than actual occupancy, which could mask real presence alerts or indicate a network configuration issue worth troubleshooting.

The sustained count of 22-27 devices alongside zero camera activity strongly suggests network signal bleed or a presence detection anomaly rather than actual occupancy, as a gathering of that size would typically trigger at least some camera motion; this discrepancy risks triggering incorrect automation or false security alerts.

The sustained presence of ~27 mobile devices alongside zero camera activity during a Friday evening strongly indicates an unmonitored gathering, likely occurring in camera-blind zones or with cameras disabled. This creates a security gap Steve should verify before assuming normal household activity.

Since cameras show no activity and it's a weekday afternoon, verifying the actual device count will help rule out unauthorized access or automation drift.

The stable 26–29 device count combined with zero camera motion throughout the night confirms normal overnight behavior for a highly automated home, indicating all residents and pets are asleep with no signs of network instability or unauthorized activity.
